blocks.text: An identity provider (IdP) is a service that stores and manages user identity and authenticates users to access applications. IdPs work with single sign-on (SSO) providers to authenticate users. An SSO is a service that enables users to sign in once to access all their applications.

When configuring SAML for users, you can configure only one identity provider (IdP) for your organization. The Zscaler service redirects users to the SAML URL based on the configured IdP criteria. You can configure just-in-time (JIT) provisioning and IdP-initiated SSO. To learn more, see About SAML and Adding an IdP Configuration.
You can add only one IdP configuration for a single tenant.
On the Identity Provider page (Administration > Single Sign On), you can:

blocks.item: View the following details after you add an IdP:
Status: The status (Enabled or Disabled) of the IdP.
Identity Provider Issuer: The URL of the IdP issuer.

blocks.text: After you add one IdP configuration, the Add IdP Configuration button is not visible. However, you can edit an IdP configuration or delete an IdP configuration as required.
